issues: The valley is given as the setting, but the verses only say these events occurred while Nephi’s father dwelt there; they do not explicitly place the group or narrator at the tent or valley.
The verse does not explicitly place Lehi at the tent when the voice speaks by night; the tent location is inferred from surrounding context.
Verse 11 refers to the gathering group as “we” without naming its individual members; the listed characters are plausible from context but not individually specified in this verse.
Verse 12 refers to the departing group as “we” and does not identify each listed individual as present.
Verse 13 refers to the travelers as “we” and does not identify each listed individual as present.
Verse 17 says “we” pitched tents but does not identify each listed individual as present.
The verse identifies Nephi’s angry “brethren” collectively, not Sam or Zoram individually; listing them as present invents which people were there.
The verse says the travelers returned to “our families” but does not identify every traveler or family member present; the listed individuals are inferred from context.
The verse says Nephi’s “brethren” afflicted him but does not identify them individually; listing Sam and the sons of Ishmael as present goes beyond the verse.
The verses say “they” humbled themselves without specifying every person; the listed group members are inferred from context.
The verse refers to Nephi’s “brethren” without identifying them individually; the named brothers in the character list are not individually established as present in this moment.
The verse says “we” pitched tents and does not specify the travelers’ number or individual identities.
The verse says the Lord blessed “us” with food but does not describe the food’s source or its visible arrival; avoid depicting a specific means of provision.
